<!-- EDIT: say which nb-boostmtree_fit job in this set this explains, and what
     question the importance and effect plots are meant to answer. -->

Explains the fit the `nb-boostmtree_fit` job in this set saved.

An `nb-boostmtree_explain` job never fits. It reads `nb-boostmtree_fit.rds`,
which the fit job writes, and reports variable importance over repeated runs,
partial effects over time and a sample of patients' fitted trajectories, all of
that saved fit and no other. Each importance run is cached on its own, so
raising N_VIMP pays only for the new runs.

<!-- The two values below are written by add_job() from the subject/type it
     was called with, which are also the filename's first two fields. They
     name the SET this job belongs to, and every artifact path in the
     document is computed from them, so no output path below needs editing.

     Do NOT hand-edit these declarations: the render-time guard below checks
     them against this file's own name and stops if they disagree. To put
     this job in a different set, call add_job() again with the new
     subject/type rather than editing this copy in place.

     A set is keyed on (subject, analysis type), not on the subject alone.
     One subject may be analyzed by several methods, such as parametric hazard,
     random forest survival or competing risks, and those chains share their upstream.
     Two sets keyed on `dead` alone would write their life tables to the
     same file. -->


```{r}
#| label: setup
#| results: asis
SUBJECT <- "lvef"
TYPE    <- "boost"
.in <- knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)
# boostmtree must be the CCF fork, 2.0.13 or later. Every study fits with
# cv.flag = TRUE, and in boostmtree 2.0.0 (the CRAN release) that flag leaves the
# in-sample fit frozen, so the stored coefficients diverge with M and every
# non-cross-validated result is wrong (kogalur/boostmtree#2, fixed by #3). 2.0.13
# is the floor because it is the release whose seed reproduces a fit: before it,
# the same SEED could grow a different fit. A seed reproduces a fit only within one
# randomForestSRC version, which is why the saved fit records that version too.
# 2.0.8 added the progress = argument and the lower worker memory this job relies on.
if (!requireNamespace("boostmtree", quietly = TRUE) || utils::packageVersion("boostmtree") < "2.0.13") {
  stop("This job needs boostmtree >= 2.0.13 from the CCF fork. Install it with\n",
       "  remotes::install_github(\"ehrlinger/boostmtree_src\", subdir = \"boostmtree\", ref = \"v2.0.13-ccf\")\n",
       "then re-render.", call. = FALSE)
}
# ggBoostedTrees 0.10.2 adds the pooled importance this job reads (gg_boost_vimp() on
# a list of runs). The floor is 0.10.3 because the fit job needs that release's
# boost_shadow() fix, and the pair installs together.
if (!requireNamespace("ggBoostedTrees", quietly = TRUE) || utils::packageVersion("ggBoostedTrees") < "0.10.3") {
  stop("This job needs ggBoostedTrees >= 0.10.3. Install it with\n",
       "  remotes::install_github(\"ehrlinger/ggBoostedTrees@v0.10.3\")\nthen re-render.", call. = FALSE)
}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(boostmtree)
  library(ggBoostedTrees)
  library(hvtiRutilities)
})
# Without the guard in .job_setup(), an unedited job renders green over a
# meaningless analysis. Here that is importance and effects drawn for a fit this
# job was never pointed at, which look exactly like a result.
# To render a job you have not finished, leave a chunk out with the chunk
# option skip, giving the reason in quotes, or call hvtiRtemplates::stop_here()
# in a chunk to leave out everything below it. A draft lists each one in a
# callout; a final render refuses them, as it refuses an unresolved marker.
# ?stop_here has more.
.job <- hvtiRtemplates:::.job_setup(SUBJECT, TYPE, envir = environment())
.root <- .job$root
set_path <- .job$set_path
.provenance_data <- list()
# Saves a figure as <name>.png, .pdf and .tiff in this set's graphs/ folder (or `kind`'s),
# under the SAVE_FIGURES and FIGURES study choices.
save_figure <- function(plot, name, width = 6, height = 4, kind = "graphs", linked = FALSE) {
  hvtiRtemplates:::.save_figure(plot, set_path(kind, paste0(name, ".png")), width, height,
                                SAVE_FIGURES, FIGURES, linked)
}

# The importance runs and partial effects are cached through set_path(), by set,
# beside the fit this job reads, and no other set's.
# The draft banners, if any, and the box under the title, after all the code above.
.job$notice
```

## Study choices

Edit these values for this study before rendering. The response, visit time,
predictors, iterations, shadows and refits are not here: they come from the fit.

```{r}
#| label: edit-study-choices
# EDIT: the fit's selection is used; set any of these only to confirm it.
# NULL takes the value the fit job used.
WHERE <- NULL
ID <- NULL
KEY <- NULL

# EDIT: importance runs on each fit the fit job saved (the SEED fit and its
# N_REFITS refits), so N_VIMP * (1 + N_REFITS) in all. Each run permutes every
# predictor once at random; repeated runs show how stable a verdict is. A share of
# runs is stability, not significance: there is no error rate behind it. Each run
# costs about 0.17 of a fit at K_SHADOW = 5 (measured at 100 patients). Each is
# cached on its own, so raising N_VIMP pays only for the new runs. With no shadows
# in the fit there is no band to judge runs against, and importance runs once.
# With EFFECT_VARIABLES <- NULL, raising N_VIMP can change which six variables lead,
# and the partial-effects cache then stops the render until REFIT <- TRUE, which
# recomputes them and so needs run_job(); the importance runs themselves are reused.
N_VIMP <- 10

# EDIT: cores for the importance runs, one run per core. Each core is a forked copy
# of R holding the fit, so memory limits CORES on a large study. Not part of any
# cache key: cache_fit() seeds every run, so results do not depend on it.
CORES <- if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows") 1L else 4L

# EDIT: seeds the importance runs, run j on fit i under SEED + j + 1000 * i (the SEED
# fit is fit 0), so no two runs share a permutation, and the sample of patients the
# trajectory plot draws. Part of every cache key.
SEED <- 2026

# EDIT: the variables to draw partial effects for, or NULL for the six with the
# largest median importance across runs. N_TRACES patients are sampled for the
# trajectory plot; Inf draws every one.
EFFECT_VARIABLES <- NULL
N_TRACES <- 100

# Set TRUE after changing a choice above. A cache whose inputs changed stops the
# render instead of returning the old fit; TRUE recomputes it.
REFIT <- FALSE

# Each figure is saved to graphs/ as a PNG (for Word) and a PDF (for the publisher), and as a TIFF when ragg is installed.
# SAVE_FIGURES <- FALSE saves none; FIGURES keeps only the figures whose names
# start with one of its entries, e.g. FIGURES <- c("nb-boostmtree_explain-importance"). The names are the
# file names, listed for each template in the templates README.
SAVE_FIGURES <- TRUE
FIGURES <- NULL
```

## The fit

```{r}
#| label: fit
#| results: asis
.handoff <- set_path("estimates", "nb-boostmtree_fit.rds")
if (!file.exists(.handoff)) {
  stop("No fit at ", .handoff, ". Render the nb-boostmtree_fit job in this set first; ",
       "this job explains that fit and never fits its own.", call. = FALSE)
}
.cfg <- study_config(start = .root)
# Read through .read_handoff(), never readRDS(): it validates the lineage the fit
# job attached, and a final render refuses a fit saved from unregistered data.
.fit_read <- hvtiRtemplates:::.read_handoff(.handoff, "fit", .cfg, "the nb-boostmtree_fit job")
.bundle <- .fit_read$value
.provenance_data <- .fit_read$lineage$data
.provenance_artifacts <- c(.fit_read$lineage$artifacts, list(.fit_read$record))
.missing <- setdiff(c("fit", "refits", "versions", "k_shadow", "seed"), names(.bundle))
if (length(.missing)) {
  stop("nb-boostmtree_fit.rds lacks ", paste(.missing, collapse = ", "), ". Render the nb-boostmtree_fit job in this set ",
       "again.", call. = FALSE)
}
fit <- .bundle$fit
if (!(inherits(fit, "boostmtree") && inherits(fit, "grow"))) {
  stop("nb-boostmtree_fit.rds does not hold a (boostmtree, grow) fit. Render the nb-boostmtree_fit job in this set ",
       "again.", call. = FALSE)
}
refits <- .bundle$refits
CACHE_DIR <- dirname(.handoff)
.response <- .fit_read$lineage$analysis$response
.time <- .fit_read$lineage$analysis$time
# The fit's real predictors; its shadow copies are named shadow<j>.<predictor>.
.predictors <- fit$x.var.names[!grepl("^shadow[0-9]+[.]", fit$x.var.names)]
# Importance pushes permuted data down the saved trees, and that path runs
# through randomForestSRC, so a run under other versions may not match one under
# the fit's. Said in the report and as a warning, not refused.
.recorded <- .bundle$versions[c("boostmtree", "randomForestSRC")]
.installed <- vapply(names(.recorded), function(p) format(utils::packageVersion(p)), character(1L))
.moved <- names(.recorded)[.recorded != .installed]
if (length(.moved)) {
  .msg <- paste0("The fit was grown with ", paste(.moved, .recorded[.moved], collapse = " and "),
                 "; this session has ", paste(.moved, .installed[.moved], collapse = " and "),
                 ". Importance runs through randomForestSRC on the saved trees, so these runs may not match ",
                 "one on the fit's versions. Render nb-boostmtree_fit again to grow the fit on these.")
  cat("::: {.callout-warning}\n", .msg, "\n:::\n\n", sep = "")
  warning(.msg, call. = FALSE)
}
# Each component is named by the level that defines it, which boostmtree keeps
# in fit$q.set: a threshold for an ordinal fit, a class compared against the
# reference class for a binary or nominal one. partial.plot() selects a
# component by the same label ("response" for a continuous fit).
.labels <- if (identical(fit$family, "continuous")) "response" else as.character(fit$q.set)
.reference <- setdiff(as.character(fit$y.levels), .labels)
# An ordinal component is a cumulative logit at its threshold, but boostmtree's
# documentation does not say which side of the threshold it models, so the
# label names the threshold only. (Its 2.0.2 source codes P(y <= k); read the
# installed package before relying on that.)
.components <- switch(fit$family,
  continuous = .response,
  binary = ,
  nominal = paste(.response, "=", .labels, "against", paste(.reference, collapse = ", ")),
  ordinal = paste(.response, "threshold", .labels)
)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-data
#| tbl-cap: "The data the fit job read"
# This job reads no data: the fit carries its training rows. The fit job
# recorded how it chose them, and a setting above that differs from the fit's
# stops here rather than describe rows the fit was not grown on.
.sel <- hvtiRtemplates:::.read_upstream_job_data(
  .cfg, .fit_read$lineage, list(where = WHERE, id = ID, key = KEY), read = FALSE, source = "nb-boostmtree_fit.rds"
)$selection
knitr::kable(data.frame(step = c("ID", "KEY", "WHERE", "Rows"),
                        value = c(.sel$id, paste(.sel$key, collapse = ", "),
                                  if (length(.sel$where_shown)) paste(.sel$where_shown, collapse = "; ") else "none",
                                  .sel$rows)),
             col.names = c("Data", ""))
```

## Importance

```{r}
#| label: fig-importance
#| fig-cap: "Importance of each predictor's main effect and of its interaction with time, one panel for each. With shadow
#|   covariates, each box spans the 25th to 75th percentile of a predictor's margin over its own run's noise band
#|   across runs, the whiskers the 15th to 85th, each point is one run, the label k/N counts the runs in which it
#|   cleared the band, and the vertical line marks zero. Without shadows, horizontal dark gray bars give one run's
#|   importance."
#| fig-width: 9.75
#| fig-height: 10.5
# vimp.boostmtree() permutes each predictor at random, so one run's verdict on a
# predictor near the noise band can land on either side of it. Each fit gets
# N_VIMP runs, run j on fit i seeded SEED + j + 1000 * i and cached on its own, and the runs are
# pooled: each is judged against its own band, never a pooled one.
if (!is.numeric(N_VIMP) || length(N_VIMP) != 1L || is.na(N_VIMP) || N_VIMP < 1 || N_VIMP > 999 || N_VIMP != round(N_VIMP)) {
  # At most 999, so the seeds below, SEED + j + 1000 * i, never coincide across fits.
  stop("N_VIMP must be a whole number from 1 to 999, the importance runs on each fit.", call. = FALSE)
}
.fits <- c(list(fit0 = fit), stats::setNames(refits, sprintf("fit%d", seq_along(refits))))
# Without shadows there is no band to pool against, so importance runs once, on the SEED fit.
if (.bundle$k_shadow == 0) .fits <- .fits["fit0"]
.n_vimp <- if (.bundle$k_shadow > 0) as.integer(N_VIMP) else 1L
.runs_plan <- data.frame(fit = rep(names(.fits), each = .n_vimp), run = rep(seq_len(.n_vimp), times = length(.fits)),
                         stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
.runs_plan$name <- paste0(.runs_plan$fit, ".run", .runs_plan$run)
# Run j on fit i is seeded SEED + j + 1000 * i, so no two runs share a seed: vimp.boostmtree() permutes with
# sample(), and one seed across the fits would give every fit the same permutations. fit0 keeps SEED + j.
.runs_plan$seed <- SEED + .runs_plan$run + 1000L * (match(.runs_plan$fit, names(.fits)) - 1L)
.runs_plan$cache <- sprintf("nb-boostmtree_explain-vimp-%s-run%d", .runs_plan$fit, .runs_plan$run)
.vimp_code <- quote(vimp.boostmtree(f))
# Refuses here, before any run, importance this session's memory cannot hold, and a run that will be computed
# from the Render button or a terminal, where it dies with the session. Whether cache_fit() will run is its
# own decision, asked the way it makes it. Each worker holds a fitted model, so the estimate is the fit's,
# which is conservative for importance and has not been measured for it.
.need <- function(k) hvtiRtemplates:::.boostmtree_need_gib(fit$n, sum(fit$ni), fit$family, k, fit$M)
.computing <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(.runs_plan)), function(i) {
  # Bound as .vimp_run() binds it: the key takes `f` from this frame, and without it a current cache reads as stale.
  f <- .fits[[.runs_plan$fit[[i]]]]
  hvtiRutilities::cache_would_fit(.runs_plan$cache[[i]], .vimp_code, seed = .runs_plan$seed[[i]], dir = CACHE_DIR,
                                  refit = REFIT, packages = "randomForestSRC")
}, logical(1L))
if (any(.computing)) {
  hvtiRtemplates::guard_long_fit(.runs_plan$cache[.computing], dir = CACHE_DIR,
                                 why = "repeated boostmtree importance takes hours at study size", refit = REFIT)
}
hvtiRtemplates::guard_memory(if (any(.computing)) .need(CORES) else 0,
                             sprintf("these importance runs (%s patients, %s visits, %s)",
                                     format(fit$n, big.mark = ","), format(sum(fit$ni), big.mark = ","), fit$family),
                             cores = CORES, cores_fit = .need)
.vimp_run <- function(i) {
  f <- .fits[[.runs_plan$fit[[i]]]]
  # One randomForestSRC thread per forked worker, so CORES runs use CORES threads.
  if (CORES > 1L) withr::local_options(rf.cores = 1L)
  # randomForestSRC runs under boostmtree and neither call names it, so it is keyed here.
  cache_fit(.runs_plan$cache[[i]], .vimp_code, seed = .runs_plan$seed[[i]], dir = CACHE_DIR, refit = REFIT,
            packages = "randomForestSRC")
}
.runs <- if (CORES > 1L) {
  parallel::mclapply(seq_len(nrow(.runs_plan)), .vimp_run, mc.cores = CORES)
} else {
  lapply(seq_len(nrow(.runs_plan)), .vimp_run)
}
# A worker that was killed, out of memory for one, returns NULL rather than an error.
.lost <- which(vapply(.runs, is.null, logical(1L)))
if (length(.lost)) {
  stop("The importance run ", .runs_plan$name[[.lost[[1L]]]], " returned nothing: its worker was probably killed, ",
       "most often for want of memory. Lower CORES and render again; the runs already cached are kept.", call. = FALSE)
}
# mclapply() returns an error as a value; raise the first one as it was, its class
# included, so a stale cache still names what changed.
.failed <- which(vapply(.runs, inherits, logical(1L), "try-error"))
if (length(.failed)) stop(attr(.runs[[.failed[[1L]]]], "condition"))
names(.runs) <- .runs_plan$name
.pool <- if (.bundle$k_shadow > 0) gg_boost_vimp(.runs) else NULL
p_vimp <- plot(if (is.null(.pool)) gg_boost_vimp(.runs[[1L]]) else .pool) + hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12)
save_figure(p_vimp, "nb-boostmtree_explain-importance", width = 6.5, height = 7)
p_vimp
```

```{r}
#| label: importance-runs
#| results: asis
# unnumbered: its child chunk carries its own label and caption
importance_table <- NULL
if (is.null(.pool)) {
  cat("The fit has no shadow covariates (K_SHADOW was 0 in nb-boostmtree_fit), so no noise band and no share could ",
      "be computed, and importance ran once. The figure shows that one run; a predictor's place in it is not a ",
      "verdict.\n\n", sep = "")
} else {
  importance_table <- .pool[, c("variable", "component", "response", "n_detected", "n_runs", "share",
                                "median_importance", "q25", "q75")]
  class(importance_table) <- "data.frame"
  cat(sprintf(paste("Importance pools %d runs on %s, %d in all. For each predictor and panel the table gives the",
                    "runs in which its importance exceeded its shadows (that run's noise band), their share, the",
                    "median importance and the 25th and 75th percentiles of the margin over the band. The share says",
                    "how stable a single run's verdict is, not whether the effect is real. In a 50-seed study, some",
                    "covariates cleared their run's noise band in 14%% to 46%% of runs.\n\n"),
              .n_vimp, if (length(.fits) == 1L) "1 fit" else sprintf("each of %d fits", length(.fits)),
              nrow(.runs_plan)))
  .fence <- strrep("`", 3)
  cat(knitr::knit_child(text = c(
    paste0(.fence, "{r}"), "#| label: tbl-importance",
    "#| tbl-cap: \"How often each predictor cleared its run's noise band, by panel\"",
    paste("knitr::kable(importance_table, digits = 3, col.names = c('Predictor', 'Effect', 'Response', 'Runs cleared',",
          "'Runs', 'Share', 'Median importance', 'Margin, 25th percentile', 'Margin, 75th percentile'))"),
    .fence
  ), envir = environment(), quiet = TRUE), sep = "\n")
}
```

## Partial effects

```{r}
#| label: effects
#| results: asis
# unnumbered: each child chunk below carries its own label and caption
# Partial effects over time, on the SEED fit, for EFFECT_VARIABLES or the six
# with the largest median importance across runs (the first run's importance
# when the fit has no shadows), so the pages do not reshuffle between renders.
# An ordinal or nominal fit reports importance once per response component, so a
# variable is ranked by its largest importance across them.
if (is.null(.pool)) {
  .vimp_main <- gg_boost_vimp(.runs[[1L]], components = "main")
  .top <- sort(tapply(.vimp_main$importance, as.character(.vimp_main$variable), max), decreasing = TRUE)
} else {
  .vimp_main <- .pool[.pool$component == "main", ]
  .top <- sort(tapply(.vimp_main$median_importance, as.character(.vimp_main$variable), max), decreasing = TRUE)
}
.effect_vars <- if (is.null(EFFECT_VARIABLES)) head(names(.top), 6L) else EFFECT_VARIABLES
.unknown <- setdiff(.effect_vars, .predictors)
if (length(.unknown)) stop("EFFECT_VARIABLES names no predictor: ", paste(.unknown, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
# One partial.plot() covers every response component: ggBoostedTrees 0.9.0 and
# later take an ordinal or nominal one whole and facet its figure by component.
# Each component is renamed as the fit summary names it, not by its bare level.
.fence <- strrep("`", 3)
.seen <- new.env()
.child <- function(label, caption, code, opts = NULL) {
  label <- gsub("(^-+|-+$)", "", gsub("[^a-z0-9]+", "-", tolower(label)))
  if (!is.null(.seen[[label]])) stop("Two outputs would share the label ", label, ".", call. = FALSE)
  .seen[[label]] <- TRUE
  .opt <- paste0("#| ", sub("-.*$", "", label), "-cap: ", encodeString(caption, quote = "\""))
  cat(knitr::knit_child(text = c(paste0(.fence, "{r}"), paste0("#| label: ", label), .opt, opts, code, .fence),
                        envir = parent.frame(), quiet = TRUE), sep = "\n")
  cat("\n")
}
# partial.plot() is the slowest step after the fit: one prediction over every
# patient per grid value, 25 values per continuous covariate. It is cached
# beside the fit and keyed on it, so a re-render that changes only prose skips
# it, and a refit or a changed EFFECT_VARIABLES stops until REFIT, as the fit does.
# Quoted once, so the check below and cache_fit() read the same call.
.partial_code <- quote(partial.plot(fit, x.var.names = .effect_vars, output = "data", verbose = FALSE,
                                    progress = get(".job")$progress("prediction")))
# Guarded on its own, because the importance runs may all load while this recomputes, as after a changed
# EFFECT_VARIABLES. partial.plot() forks no workers, so its need is the fit's at one core whatever CORES is, an
# estimate not measured for prediction. Both guards sit inside the `if`: a guard_memory() of 0 here would overwrite
# the need the importance runs recorded for job_status().
if (hvtiRutilities::cache_would_fit("nb-boostmtree_explain-partial", .partial_code, seed = SEED, dir = CACHE_DIR,
                                    refit = REFIT, packages = "randomForestSRC")) {
  hvtiRtemplates::guard_long_fit("nb-boostmtree_explain-partial", dir = CACHE_DIR, refit = REFIT,
                                 why = "the partial effects predict over every patient at each grid value")
  hvtiRtemplates::guard_memory(.need(1L), sprintf("the partial effects (%s patients, %s visits, %s)",
                                                  format(fit$n, big.mark = ","), format(sum(fit$ni), big.mark = ","),
                                                  fit$family))
}
# randomForestSRC runs under boostmtree and neither call names it, so it is keyed here.
.partial <- cache_fit("nb-boostmtree_explain-partial", .partial_code, seed = SEED, dir = CACHE_DIR, refit = REFIT,
                      packages = "randomForestSRC")
.effect <- gg_boost_effect(.partial)
.relabel <- .components[match(levels(.effect$response), .labels)]
# A component ggBoostedTrees names differently from the fit would otherwise be
# drawn under a blank label; stop and say so instead.
if (anyNA(.relabel)) {
  stop("ggBoostedTrees labels a response component this job does not recognize: ",
       paste(levels(.effect$response)[is.na(.relabel)], collapse = ", "), ".", call. = FALSE)
}
levels(.effect$response) <- .relabel
# What ggBoostedTrees 0.9.0 still cannot do: a continuous covariate is drawn as
# a curve and a factor as a point per level, on axes ggplot2 cannot share, so
# plot() refuses an effect holding both. Each kind is drawn in its own figure,
# which is why p_effects is a list.
.discrete <- tapply(!is.na(.effect$x_label), .effect$variable, any)
.discrete <- .discrete[!is.na(.discrete)]
.parts <- split(names(.discrete), .discrete)
.kinds <- ifelse(names(.parts) == "TRUE", "categorical", "continuous")
# Free size, paged: one facet per predictor, two by two on a page no larger than
# 6.5 by 9 in. With several response components ggBoostedTrees draws one column
# per predictor and one row per component, so a page holds two predictors.
.n_components <- nlevels(.effect$response)
.pages <- lapply(unname(.parts), function(v) {
  if (.n_components > 1L) {
    hvtiRtemplates:::.figure_pages(length(v), panel_height = 3 * .n_components, page_height = 3 * .n_components)
  } else {
    hvtiRtemplates:::.figure_pages(length(v), page_height = 6)
  }
})
# One plot per page, kind by kind: p_effects holds every page, and .effect_page says which kind and page each is.
p_effects <- list()
.effect_page <- list()
for (.k in seq_along(.parts)) {
  for (.j in seq_along(.pages[[.k]])) {
    part <- .effect[.effect$variable %in% .parts[[.k]][.pages[[.k]][[.j]]$index], , drop = FALSE]
    part$variable <- droplevels(part$variable)
    # The manuscript theme hides the legend and its title, and the caption reads the time colors from the legend.
    p_effects[[length(p_effects) + 1L]] <- plot(part) +
      hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12, legend.position = "top", legend.title = ggplot2::element_text())
    .effect_page[[length(.effect_page) + 1L]] <- list(kind = .kinds[[.k]], page = .j, of = length(.pages[[.k]]),
                                                      size = .pages[[.k]][[.j]], vars = levels(part$variable))
  }
}
.key <- c(continuous = paste("Each solid line is the effect at one follow-up time, colored from dark to light blue by",
                             "time as in the color bar."),
          categorical = paste("Each point is the effect at one level and follow-up time, colored from dark to light blue by",
                              "time as in the color bar."))
for (.i in seq_along(p_effects)) {
  .p <- p_effects[[.i]]
  .pg <- .effect_page[[.i]]
  save_figure(.p, sprintf("nb-boostmtree_explain-effects-%s-page-%02d", .pg$kind, .pg$page),
              width = .pg$size$width, height = .pg$size$height)
  .on_page <- if (.pg$of > 1L) paste0(" Page ", .pg$page, " of ", .pg$of, ": ", paste(.pg$vars, collapse = ", "), ".") else ""
  .child(paste("fig effects", .pg$kind, .pg$page),
         paste0("Partial effects over follow-up, ", .pg$kind, " predictors, one panel per predictor. ", .key[[.pg$kind]],
                .on_page),
         ".p", opts = c(sprintf("#| fig-width: %g", hvtiRtemplates:::.report_size(.pg$size$width)),
                        sprintf("#| fig-height: %g", hvtiRtemplates:::.report_size(.pg$size$height))))
}
```

## Trajectories

```{r}
#| label: fig-traces
#| fig-cap: "Fitted trajectories for a sample of patients, with the cohort's mean fitted value over time. Thin translucent
#|   black lines trace each sampled patient's fitted values, translucent black circles their observed values, and the
#|   thick black line the cohort's mean fitted value within ten time bins."
# Fitted trajectories for a sample of patients, with their observed values as
# points, and the cohort's mean fitted value over time drawn across them. The
# patients are labeled by digest, so none is identified.
traces <- gg_boost_trajectory(fit)
# Visit times are irregular, so most exact times belong to one patient, and a
# mean taken at each time would join single values. The mean is taken instead
# within ten equal-count time bins, over every patient's fitted values, and
# drawn at each bin's mean time. A bin is per response component when there
# are several.
.edges <- unique(stats::quantile(traces$time, seq(0, 1, length.out = 11L), names = FALSE))
# plot() reports that it chose the patients at random; SEED makes the choice
# the same on every render.
p_traces <- withr::with_seed(SEED, plot(traces, n_max = N_TRACES)) + ggplot2::labs(x = .time, y = .response) +
  hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12)
if (length(.edges) < 2L) {
  # Every visit at one time leaves no span to bin, and no line to draw.
  trace_means <- NULL
  cat("Every visit is at one time, so no mean line is drawn.\n")
} else {
  traces$.bin <- cut(traces$time, .edges, include.lowest = TRUE)
  .by <- intersect(c("response", ".bin"), names(traces))
  trace_means <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(traces, traces[.by], drop = TRUE), function(b) {
    data.frame(b[1L, setdiff(.by, ".bin"), drop = FALSE], time = mean(b$time), fitted = mean(b$fitted),
               n_patients = length(unique(b$id)))
  }))
  p_traces <- p_traces +
    ggplot2::geom_line(data = trace_means, ggplot2::aes(x = .data[["time"]], y = .data[["fitted"]]),
                       linewidth = 1.2, inherit.aes = FALSE)
}
save_figure(p_traces, "nb-boostmtree_explain-traces")
p_traces
```
